messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.inference.com>
To: Elena Morris <elena@starlighthealth.com>, Jason Lee <jason.lee@starlighthealth.com>

Subject: Cloud procurement options & preferred buy path — follow-up (AWS Marketplace vs PO)

Thanks again for carving out time today — helpful call. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment on procurement and commercial path: 

TL;DR: Starlight prefers vendor-managed invoicing, procurement leaning toward PO. You indicated interest in AWS Marketplace for consolidated billing but need to confirm if a Private Offer is required for your legal team.

Call notes:
- Use case: inference for clinical summarization (low-latency, HIPAA-scope).
- Expected start: pilot in ~4–6 weeks, production on 2–3 month timeline if procurement clears.
- Consumption estimate: ~200–500k tokens/day initially (we’ll produce a quick cost projection).
- Procurement signals: Jason prefers a PO-based flow (invoice + net30) but likes Marketplace for single-vendor billing if Private Offer available.
- Compliance asks: SOC 2 report and contract CLIN redline window (legal needs ~7–10 business days).

Open questions / asks for your team:
1) Can you confirm whether Finance requires a vendor PO on file, or would Marketplace billing (AWS consolidated invoice) suffice?
2) If PO required, will you use your standard PO template or need Redwood's PO template? (I attached ours for reference.)
3) Does Legal prefer a Private Offer (AWS) that we can publish for your account, or do you want to buy via credit card to move faster for the pilot?

Proposed next steps:
- I’ll send the SOC2 summary and a short PO template (attached) by EOD. (ACTION: Priyom)
- If you confirm PO preference, we’ll draft a Private Offer/PO-ready quote and route to our finance team for Net30 terms. (ACTION: Redwood + Starlight procurement)
- Schedule a 30-min follow-up next week to confirm the buy path and sign off on timelines. (ACTION: All)

Attachments: Redwood_PO_Template.docx; SOC2-summary.pdf

Thanks —
Priyom Das
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Jason Lee <jason.lee@starlighthealth.com>

Date: 2026-06-16T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Cloud procurement options & preferred buy path — follow-up (AWS Marketplace vs PO)

Thanks, Priyom — quick answers from Procurement side below.

- Our preference is PO + Net30 rather than credit card for anything above $25k ARR. That said, for pilot (< $5k) we can process via card to speed things up if you need it.
- We are open to AWS Marketplace if Redwood can offer a Private Offer or Private Offer + PO flow; consolidated invoice with our AWS account is preferred from a bookkeeping standpoint.
- Legal: will need SOC 2 (Type II) and standard indemnity language; will push redlines within 7–10 business days once we have the draft.
- Timeline: Procurement lead time is typically 3–4 weeks for PO issuance once we have a finalized quote and W-9/PO template.

We can aim for a pilot start the week of July 6 if quoting and legal are aligned.

Regards,
Jason Lee
Senior Procurement Manager, Starlight Health
jason.lee@starlighthealth.com

Subject: Re: Cloud procurement options & preferred buy path — follow-up (internal)

Adding internal notes and recommended path so we stay coordinated before we send formal docs to Starlight.

Internal assessment:
- If Starlight wants consolidated AWS billing + PO, the cleanest flow is AWS Private Offer with a Redwood-managed listing tied to their account. That supports a PO/invoice flow and keeps bookkeeping on AWS but requires partner ops to open the Private Offer (2–5 business days).
- Alternative: direct Redwood invoice (Net30) — doable under our current Standard Terms, ~3–5 business days to generate quote + invoice. Good for pilots but not ideal for long-term centralized billing on their cloud account.
- For pilot speed: suggest we offer two parallel options in the quote: 1) Pilot via CC (card) for immediate access; 2) PO + Private Offer as the preferred production path. This reduces friction and gives Procurement a clear next step.

Action items (internal):
- Priyom: send SOC2-summary + Redwood_PO_Template.docx to Jason and Elena (done).
- Marissa: prepare a papered quote with two options (card pilot / PO private-offer) and include estimated committed rates and a 90-day review cadence.
- Karthik: reach out to partner ops to start the Private Offer request once Starlight confirms account email.

I attached our PO template for reference and drafted the language we typically use for Private Offer quotes.

Karthik
Head of Sales Operations, Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.inference.com

Appreciate the quick turnaround, Jason — good clarity. Confirming next steps and owner list so nothing falls through the cracks: 

1) Pilot execution (fast path): we can provision a card-based pilot within 3 business days if Starlight wants to accelerate. (Owner: Priyom)
2) Preferred production path: PO + AWS Private Offer so your finance team gets consolidated billing. (Owner: Redwood Sales Ops + Starlight Procurement)
3) Legal/Compliance: I attached the SOC2-summary and our PO template for your legal team to review. We’ll route full Type II upon NDA/secure link request. (Owner: Priyom / Marissa)
4) Timeline checkpoint: draft quote and Private Offer request to partner ops once you confirm the exact AWS payer account email (Owner: Karthik). If we get that this week, we’ll target a Private Offer in ~3 business days and PO issuance within ~10 business days.

Please reply with: (a) whether you want to start the pilot on card, and (b) the AWS payer account email if you want the Private Offer route. Happy to hop on a 20-minute sync tomorrow if helpful.

Thanks — looking forward to moving this along.
